hints: Use logarithm laws to turn the exponential equation into a linear equation in $x$.
Taking logs gives $(3x-1)\ln2=\ln5+(1-x)\ln3$; expand and collect the $x$-terms.
Before forming the requested quotient, combine sums of logarithms with $\ln u+\ln v=\ln(uv)$.
walkthrough:
Take the natural logarithm of both sides of the equation $2^{3x - 1} = 5(3^{1 - x})$:
$$\ln\left(2^{3x - 1}\right) = \ln\left(5 \times 3^{1 - x}\right)$$

Apply the power and product rules of logarithms:
$$(3x - 1)\ln 2 = \ln 5 + \ln\left(3^{1 - x}\right)$$
$$(3x - 1)\ln 2 = \ln 5 + (1 - x)\ln 3$$

Expand both sides of the equation:
$$3x\ln 2 - \ln 2 = \ln 5 + \ln 3 - x\ln 3$$

Collect terms in $x$ on the left-hand side and constants on the right-hand side:
$$3x\ln 2 + x\ln 3 = \ln 5 + \ln 3 + \ln 2$$
$$x(3\ln 2 + \ln 3) = \ln 5 + \ln 3 + \ln 2$$

Simplify the logarithmic expressions using laws of logarithms:
$$3\ln 2 = \ln(2^3) = \ln 8$$
$$3\ln 2 + \ln 3 = \ln 8 + \ln 3 = \ln(8 \times 3) = \ln 24$$
$$\ln 5 + \ln 3 + \ln 2 = \ln(5 \times 3 \times 2) = \ln 30$$

Substitute these simplified expressions back into the equation:
$$x\ln 24 = \ln 30$$

Divide by $\ln 24$ to isolate $x$ in the required form $\dfrac{\ln a}{\ln b}$ with integers $a = 30$ and $b = 24$:
$$x = \dfrac{\ln 30}{\ln 24}$$
